# infrawrench_dashboard_notification (Resource)

A recurring delivery of one whole dashboard, rendered as a PDF, to Slack, Teams or email.

At least one destination is required: a schedule with nowhere to deliver would only ever record failures. The dashboard itself decides what the PDF shows; the cadence here only decides how often it is sent.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Dashboards are not managed by this provider yet. Take the id from the
# dashboard's URL in the web app, or from `infrawrench config export`.
variable "ops_dashboard_id" {
  type = string
}

data "infrawrench_slack_installations" "workspace" {}

resource "infrawrench_slack_channel" "ops" {
  installation_id = data.infrawrench_slack_installations.workspace.installations[0].id
  channel_id      = "C0123456789"
  channel_name    = "ops"
}

# The ops dashboard lands in Slack and the leadership inbox as a PDF every
# Monday morning.
resource "infrawrench_dashboard_notification" "ops_weekly" {
  dashboard_id      = var.ops_dashboard_id
  cadence           = "weekly"
  send_day          = 1
  hour              = 9
  timezone          = "Europe/Berlin"
  slack_channel_ids = [infrawrench_slack_channel.ops.id]
  email_recipients  = ["leadership@example.com"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cadence` (String) How often the schedule fires. One of `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`.
- `dashboard_id` (String) The dashboard to send. This provider does not manage dashboards yet, so take the id from the dashboard's URL in the web app, or from the `dashboards` section of `infrawrench config export`. Changing it replaces the schedule: the route is nested under the dashboard, so there is nothing to move.
- `hour` (Number) Local hour (0 to 23) in `timezone` the delivery fires at.
- `timezone` (String) IANA zone, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. Validated server-side.

### Optional

- `attach_pdf` (Boolean) Defaults to `true`. When set, the rendered PDF is attached to each email and uploaded into the Slack message's thread. Teams always receives a summary and a link only, because incoming webhooks cannot carry files.

The Slack upload needs the Slack app installed with the `files:write` scope. An installation that predates it posts the message without the file until the app is reinstalled.
- `email_recipients` (List of String) Email addresses, at most 20. Lowercased server-side.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Defaults to `true`. A disabled schedule keeps its settings and never fires.
- `send_day` (Number) ISO day of week (1 = Monday, 7 = Sunday). Read only when `cadence` is `weekly`.

Computed as well as optional because the server stores a default in the column whatever the cadence is, and reads back null here for any cadence that does not use it.
- `send_day_of_month` (Number) Day of month, 1 to 31. Read only when `cadence` is `monthly`. A day the month doesn't have clamps to its last day, so 31 means month end everywhere.
- `slack_channel_ids` (List of String) Stored Slack channel row ids to post to: the `id` of an `infrawrench_slack_channel`, not a Slack `C…` id.
- `teams_webhook_ids` (List of String) Stored Teams webhook ids to post to, from `infrawrench_msteams_webhook`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned notification id. Import addresses it as `<dashboard_id>/<id>`, because the notification's own id is not enough to build its URL.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A notification hangs off its dashboard, so the notification id alone cannot
# build a URL. The address is <dashboard_id>/<notification_id>.
terraform import infrawrench_dashboard_notification.weekly 5e6f7a8b-9c0d-1e2f-3a4b-5c6d7e8f9a0b/3a4b5c6d-7e8f-9a0b-1c2d-3e4f5a6b7c8d
```
